Ben’s Better Biplot

A base R package to create beautiful looking biplots. Designed to work with prcomp(), princomp(), vegan::rda() (unconstrained PCA), survey::svyprcomp(), FactoMineR::PCA(), ade4::dudi.pca(), and psych::principal() objects, as well as custom score and loading matrices. The function is compatible with the base biplot() function, but offers significant enhancements including new features and full customisation of the biplot.

Features

  • Quickly create beautiful biplots from PCA results (prcomp(), princomp(), vegan::rda(), survey::svyprcomp(), FactoMineR::PCA(), ade4::dudi.pca(), psych::principal(), or custom matrices).
  • Uses base R only - no required third-party dependencies.
  • Compatible with base biplot() scaling and core arguments.
  • Streamlined top-level API with grouped styling lists (lab.args, var.args, ellipse.args/chull.args, leg.args, varimax.args) and v1.x backwards compatibility.
  • Style points by up to three groups (or group3 = "scaled" for survey::svyprcomp() weights) and colourblind-safe palette shorthands ("Okabe-Ito", "Viridis", etc.).
  • Add selective, condensed, and customisable legends.
  • Add statistical covariance or Hotelling-t confidence ellipses, convex hulls, group centroids, and radial spider lines.
  • Add circle of equilibrium contribution.
  • Plays nicely with layout(), mfrow(), par(), and returns plot coordinates invisibly for downstream base R annotations.

Installation

Install the betterbiplot package from GitHub using remotes (or devtools):

# Install betterbiplot from GitHub
remotes::install_github("benbell95/better_biplot")

# Optional: install with the vignette built (requires knitr and rmarkdown)
remotes::install_github("benbell95/better_biplot", build_vignettes = TRUE)

# Load the package
library(betterbiplot)

# View the vignette (if built)
vignette("betterbiplot")

Example

Run pca analysis and plot the results. Scale the plot, style the observations by the species, include a legend and “circle of equilibrium” on the plot.

# pca
p <- prcomp(iris[-5], scale=TRUE)
# Group
gr <- as.factor(iris[,5])
# Plot
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr, circle.eq=TRUE, legend=TRUE, title.leg="Species", lab.args=list(rotate=TRUE))
Better biplot example plot

Covariance confidence ellipses, group centroids, radial spider lines, colourblind-safe "Okabe-Ito" palette, and variable label offset:

bb_biplot(
  p, scale = 0, limx = 1.15, group = gr, col = "Okabe-Ito", alpha = 0.75,
  ellipse = TRUE, ellipse.args = list(method = "cov", level = 0.95, alpha = 0.15),
  centroids = "points", spider = TRUE,
  circle.eq = TRUE,
  var.args = list(lab.offset = 1.08),
  lab.args = list(rotate = TRUE),
  legend = TRUE, title.leg = "Species"
)
Better biplot v2.0.0 showcase

Supported PCA Objects

bb_biplot() is an S3 generic with built-in methods for the following PCA objects (none of the external packages are required to install betterbiplot):

Package Function Class Notes
stats (base R) prcomp() prcomp Supports scale, pc.biplot, varimax.rotate.
stats (base R) princomp() princomp Supports scale, pc.biplot, varimax.rotate.
vegan rda() rda Unconstrained PCA only; converted to base R scale (0 to 1) for compatibility.
survey svyprcomp() svyprcomp Requires scores = TRUE. Supports group3 = "scaled" to size points by survey weights.
FactoMineR PCA() PCA Supports scale, pc.biplot, varimax.rotate.
ade4 dudi.pca() pca Supports scale, pc.biplot, varimax.rotate.
psych principal() principal Requires scores = TRUE; plots scores and loadings directly (preserving any rotation).
Custom matrices bb_biplot(x, y) default Pass score matrix x, loading matrix y, and optional xsd. 
# vegan::rda() unconstrained PCA
r <- vegan::rda(iris[-5], scale = TRUE)
bb_biplot(r, scale = 0, group = gr, ellipse = TRUE, legend = TRUE)

# survey::svyprcomp() with survey-weight point sizing and condensed weight legend
sp <- survey::svyprcomp(~api99 + api00 + ell, design = dclus2, scale = TRUE, scores = TRUE)
bb_biplot(sp, scale = 0, group3 = "scaled", legend = TRUE)

Compatibility

bb_biplot() is designed to be compatible with the output from base R prcomp() and princomp() functions (as well as the other PCA classes listed in Supported PCA Objects), and create a biplot. It does not do the pca itself, rather it plots the results. For the plot, data is scaled in the same way as the base R biplot() function, and it also shares several arguments, so existing code should work with this function with only minor changes.

A comparison between the arguments is shown in the table below:

biplot() bb_biplot() Details
x, y x, y x should be a supported PCA object (or see section below).
var.axes variables Logical argument to plot the second set of points as arrows.
col col Colours are generated automatically, or can be specified.
cex cex, lab.args, var.args Size of data labels, variable labels, and data symbols can all be specified individually.
xlabs, ylabs xlab, ylab Axes labels (titles) are generated automatically, or can be specified. Only applies the main plot axes (e.g. bottom x axis, and left y axis).
expand var.args = list(expand = …) Adjust the size of the variable arrows.
arrow.len var.args = list(arrow.len = …) Adjust the size of the arrow heads, or suppress them.
xlim, ylim limx Plot limits for the x and y axes are generated automatically, but can be increased or decreased.
… … Additional arguments passed to the main plot.

See arguments section for a full list of available arguments and an explanation of what they do / how they work.

Data is scaled for plotting when using supported PCA objects. bb_biplot() directly supports unconstrained vegan::rda() objects and converts them to base R biplot() scaling (scale between 0 and 1) for consistency across all PCA classes. If you are used to vegan::biplot.rda()’s scaling argument, note the equivalence below:

biplot() / bb_biplot() vegan::biplot.rda() Biplot type
scale = 0 scaling = 1 ("sites") Distance biplot (site/observation distances preserved)
scale = 0.5 scaling = 3 ("symmetric") Symmetric biplot
scale = 1 (default) scaling = 2 ("species") (default) Correlation biplot (variable correlations preserved)

bb_biplot() can also scale the second set of data (variables) using pc.biplot=TRUE in the same way as biplot().

Additionally, you can apply a further rotation to the main data observations using varimax.rotate=TRUE. This uses the base R varimax() function (see ?varimax in R for details), which can be customised via varimax.args=list(normalize=TRUE, eps=1e-5), and applies to prcomp(), princomp(), vegan::rda(), survey::svyprcomp(), FactoMineR::PCA(), and ade4::dudi.pca() objects.

You can also plot other data which was not created by a supported PCA function as x and y values. x should be a matrix of at least two columns for the data (e.g. “scores”), and y should be a matrix of the variables (e.g. the rotation or loadings). Standard deviation values can also be supplied using xsd which are used to calculate the proportion of variance in the plot labels. This data will not be scaled by bb_biplot() and should be scaled before plotting.

bb_biplot() is a generic function, so it can be extended to plot other pca (or any other analysis object requiring a biplot) objects. See the source code for details.

To biplot (or not to biplot?)

By default, the reduced dataset principal components (e.g. the data observations) are plotted, with the variables (loadings) plotted on top for comparison, hence the term “biplot”. But, you can disable the second plot of variables using variables=FALSE. This can be useful if you have lots of variables, and you do not want the plot covered in variable arrows and/or labels!

You can also control which variables are plotted using var.args=list(which=...), where you can specify either the name (exact match) of the variable, or the index position. Additionally, if plotting the circle of equilibrium, you can specify that only variable arrows which extend beyond the circle are plotted. Examples:

# Disable plotting of variables
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr, variables=FALSE)
# Plot variables, but only certain ones:
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr, var.args=list(which="Petal.Length"))
# Plot variables, but only those extending beyond circle of equilibrium:
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr, circle.eq=TRUE, var.args=list(which="circle.eq"))

Grouping data

bb_biplot() allows you to use up to three groups to style the plot points, with the arguments group, group2, and group3. These are optional, and you can style the plot without using groups, but using groups makes styling easier and more intuitive.

Grouping data also allows ellipses, convex hulls, centroids, and spider lines to be plotted, as well as allowing plot legends to be added.

Group objects should be a factor, with a length that matches the number of data observations. For example, in the iris dataset, the fifth column “Species” is a grouping of the data, and this can be converted to a factor. gr <- as.factor(iris[,5]). If an object is supplied that is not a factor, the function will attempt to convert it.

group controls the colour of the plot points. However, it can also control the plot symbols if these are additionally specified, and group2 is not used. Example:

# Group 
# Changes colour of the plot points depending on the group
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr)
# Additionally change the plot symbols for each group
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr, pch=c(21, 22, 23))

Colours are generated automatically, or you can specify them using the col argument.

group2 controls the plot symbol (pch) for the plot points within each group, as specified by group and this must also be specified for group2 to work. Example:

# Fake group for use in example
gr2 <- sample.int(6L, length(iris[,5]), replace=TRUE)
# Group 2
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr, group2=gr2)

Plot symbols are generated automatically, or you can specify them using the pch argument. The number of specified symbols should be the same as the number of groupings of data used in group2. A guide to plotting symbols in R is available on my blog: Quick guide to pch symbols in R

group3 controls the size of the plot symbol (pch) for the plot points within each group, as specified by group and this must also be specified for group3 to work, but group2 is not required. For survey::svyprcomp() objects, you can also pass group3="scaled" (even without group) to scale point sizes by survey weights. Example:

# Fake group for use in example
gr3 <- sample.int(4L, length(iris[,5]), replace=TRUE)
# Group 3
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr, group2=gr2, group3=gr3)

Plot symbol sizes are generated automatically when using group3 based on the number of groupings of data used in group3, and are multiplied by cex.pt (so cex.pt adjusts the base point size).

Ellipses, Convex hulls, Centroids & Spider lines

You can add ellipses, convex hulls, group centroids, or radial spider lines to the biplot when group is specified.

To add convex hulls to the plot, use:

# Convex hulls
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr, chull=TRUE)

To add ellipses, use:

# 95% covariance confidence ellipses (default)
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr, ellipse=TRUE)
# Small-sample Hotelling-t ellipses at 90% confidence
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr, ellipse=TRUE, ellipse.args=list(method="t", level=0.90))

By default, ellipses draw bivariate normal covariance confidence regions (method="cov", level=0.95). You can switch to small-sample F / Hotelling’s T-squared ellipses with method="t", and control fill and border transparency via ellipse.args=list(alpha=0.25, border.alpha=0.9) (or chull.args).

To highlight group centroids and/or draw radial spider segments from each observation to its group centroid:

# Group centroids and spider lines with colourblind-safe Okabe-Ito palette
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr, col="Okabe-Ito", centroids=TRUE, spider=TRUE, legend=TRUE)

Legends

You can add a legend, or multiple legends to the plot based on the number of groups used. group is required for legends to work (except survey::svyprcomp() objects with group3="scaled", which can display a weight legend on their own). These are generated automatically, and will match the style of each group, and legend text is taken from the group arguments (i.e. the different factors). Legend titles are also generated automatically, although these are simply “Group” followed by the number (or "Weight" for svyprcomp() weights). You can specify your own titles for each group using the title.leg argument.

By default, legend=TRUE or legend="all" displays legends for all supplied groups. You can also select specific groups to display by passing group numbers (1, 2, 3), e.g. legend=1, legend=c(1, 3), or legend=3. For group3, the legend is condensed to show the minimum, middle, and maximum symbol sizes (including for survey::svyprcomp() with group3="scaled"). Examples:

# Legends: 1 group
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr, legend=TRUE, title.leg="Species")
# 2 groups (all)
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr, group2=gr2, legend="all", title.leg=c("Species", "second title"))
# 3 groups (all)
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr, group2=gr2, group3=gr3, legend=TRUE, title.leg=c("Species", "second title", "third"))
# Only show legend for group and group3
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr, group2=gr2, group3=gr3, legend=c(1, 3), title.leg=c("Species", "Size"))
# Only show legend for group3
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr, group2=gr2, group3=gr3, legend=3, title.leg="Size")

To control the order of legend items (as well as colour, symbol, and smallest-to-largest group3 symbol size mapping), set the factor levels on your grouping variable before plotting:

# Control legend order via factor levels (instead of alphabetical order)
gr_ord <- factor(gr_values, levels=c("low", "med", "high"))
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr_ord, legend=TRUE)

By default, the legends are placed in the right side margin. If only 1 legend is shown, it is vertically centred, whereas if multiple legends are shown, they are placed starting at the top of the y axis.

You can change the location of the legend(s) by using leg.args=list(x=..., y=...), to specify the absolute position using the main plot coordinates (even when variables are plotted), for example, to move the legends inside the plot area. You can also place the legend in the margins by extrapolating the likely coordinates, however, if using the bottom, left, or top margin, you must also change the plot margins using par(mar=c()) function before calling bb_biplot(). When using the right margin, this should happen automatically. You can also horizontally align the different legends, rather than vertically align using leg.args=list(horiz=TRUE). This only works with multiple groups. Examples:

# Legend inside plot (top left)
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr, group2=gr2, legend=TRUE, leg.args=list(horiz=TRUE, x=-3.2))
# Legend outside plot (bottom margin)
par(mar=c(12,4,4,4))
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr, group2=gr2, legend=TRUE, leg.args=list(horiz=TRUE, x=-3.2, y=-6.5))

You may need to resize the plot window and/or re-run the code to show this correctly.

Full customisation

You can customise pretty much every aspect of the plot, beyond what is mentioned in this readme file. Refer to further examples or the arguments section below for full details.

For example, try using lab.args=list(rotate=TRUE) to change how labels are plotted.

You can also use other functions to add elements to the main plot before the points are drawn (f1), and to the variables plot before the arrows & labels are drawn (f2). Pass a zero-argument function (e.g. f1 = function() supergrid(col = "grey") or f1 = supergrid).

For example, if you wanted to add a more extensive grid to the plot, you could use my supergrid() function and call this in the main function call.

# Load supergrid script from Github
source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/benbell95/supergrid/refs/heads/main/r/supergrid.r")

### data generated in previous example...
# Plot
bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr, circle.eq=TRUE, legend=TRUE, title.leg="Species", lab.args=list(rotate=TRUE), f1=supergrid)

You can also add other plot elements to the biplot (after using bb_biplot()) using the various plot functions available in R. bb_biplot() invisibly returns an object containing scores, loadings, lim, limr, pc, pvar, group_cols, and centroids to make custom annotations easy. Note that when variables=TRUE, the active plot coordinate system is limr (variable axes); reset par(usr=c(bp$lim, bp$lim)) before drawing in score/centroid coordinates, or use variables=FALSE:

bp <- bb_biplot(p, scale=0, group=gr, col="Viridis", alpha=0.6,
                var.args=list(lab.offset=1.12),
                labd=rownames(iris), lab.args=list(pos="auto"))
# Reset user coordinates to score space (bp$lim) before annotating centroids
par(usr=c(bp$lim, bp$lim))
text(bp$centroids, labels=rownames(bp$centroids), font=2)

Further examples and help

More information and detailed examples on how to use this function are available on my blog (coming soon!): benjaminbell.co.uk.

You can also access the built-in documentation in R using ?bb_biplot (or args(bb_biplot.default) to see all arguments and their default values), browse the full walkthrough in vignette("betterbiplot"), and see NEWS.md for full v2.0.0 release notes.

Arguments

Details for the available arguments are shown in the table below. Fine-grained styling options are grouped into lab.args, var.args, ellipse.args (or chull.args), leg.args, and varimax.args with sensible defaults, so you only need to override what you want to customise.

Argument Details
x Observations. Matrix with at least 2 columns. Automatically determined for supported PCA objects.
y Variables. Matrix with at least 2 columns. Automatically determined for supported PCA objects.
xsd Optional. Vector of standard deviation values for the variables. Automatically determined for supported PCA objects. (Used for automatic axis labels).
pc Integer vector of length 2 giving the principal components to plot (default = c(1, 2)).
scale Scale data between 0 and 1 for plotting (default = 1). This works the same way as R base biplot() function.
pc.biplot Logical. Additional scaling of variables (default = FALSE). This works the same way as R base biplot() function.
varimax.rotate Logical. Additionally apply varimax rotation (see ?varimax for help) (default = FALSE). Applies to prcomp, princomp, vegan::rda, survey::svyprcomp, FactoMineR::PCA, and ade4::dudi.pca objects.
varimax.args Named list of arguments passed to stats::varimax() when varimax.rotate = TRUE: normalize (logical, default TRUE) and eps (numeric tolerance, default 1e-5).
limx xlim and ylim are generated automatically, but you can increase or decrease using a multiplier value (e.g. 1.5)
grid Logical. Draw a grid through center x and y axes (default = TRUE).
col Optional. Colours for the plot / groups, or a single palette name from palette.pals() (e.g. "Okabe-Ito") or hcl.pals() (e.g. "Viridis"). Automatically generates a palette if not supplied.
pch Optional. Plotting symbols to use for the observations (also see group 2) (default symbol = 21).
cex.pt Changes the size of the plotting symbols.
alpha Point opacity in [0, 1] (default = 0.85).
xlab Overwrite the default x axis label.
ylab Overwrite the default y axis label.
axes Logical. Plot axes (This controls all axes including variables) (default = TRUE).
cex.axis Change the size of the axes, and axes labels.
cex Globally change the size of all plot elements. Multiplies default or specified size of each plot element.
group Optional. Groups for the data. Should be a factor, with length that matches original data. This affects the colour of the points and also allows for ellipses or convex hulls to be drawn. This will also affect the plot symbol used if multiple pch supplied, unless group2 is also specified where symbols will then relate to the second group.
group2 Optional. Second grouping of data. Should be a factor, with length that matches original data. This affects the pch symbol only (e.g. multiple symbols within a single grouping). group must also be specified.
group3 Optional. Third grouping of data. Should be a factor, with length that matches original data. This affects the size of the pch symbol (size automatically determined based on number of groups), and its legend is condensed to show minimum, middle, and maximum sizes. group must also be specified (but does not need group2). For survey::svyprcomp() objects, can also be set to "scaled" to scale point size by survey weights (sqrt(w / max(w)), with a condensed min/median/max weight legend when legends are enabled).
labd Optional. A vector of labels for the data observations, this should be the same length as the data. Use NA values to omit some labels.
lab.args Named list of label styling options: col (default "black"), cex (default 0.5), font (1–4, default 1), rotate (logical, default FALSE), ran.adj (logical, default FALSE), valign (0, 0.5, or 1, default 0.5), pos ("auto", "random", or 1–4, default "auto").
variables Logical. Whether to plot the variables or not (default = TRUE).
circle.eq Logical. Plot circle of equilibrium contribution (default = FALSE). Only works when scale = 0. Takes colour from var.args$col, and line width scales in proportion to var.args$lwd.
var.args Named list of variable-arrow styling options: vname (defaults to rownames(y)), which (names, indices, or "circle.eq"), expand (default 1), lab.offset (default 1.05), arrow.len (default 0.15), lwd (default 2), col (default "#d12631"), col.lab (default "black"), cex.lab (default 1), font.lab (1–4, default 1), axes (logical, default TRUE).
chull Logical. Add convex hulls to the plot - group must be supplied for this to work (default = FALSE).
ellipse Logical. Draw ellipses around the data observations based on the group (default = FALSE).
centroids Draw group centroids when group is supplied (default = FALSE). Accepts FALSE, TRUE (markers + labels), "points", or "labels".
spider Logical. Draw segments connecting each observation to its group centroid (default = FALSE).
ellipse.args Named list of hull and ellipse styling options (also accepted via alias chull.args): method ("cov" or "t", default "cov"), level (confidence level in (0, 1), default 0.95), autolim (default TRUE), nofill (default FALSE), alpha (fill opacity, default 0.25), border.alpha (border/spider opacity, default 0.9), lwd (default 2).
legend Controls legend display (default = FALSE). Accepts FALSE (none), TRUE or “all” (all supplied groups), or integer values in 1:3 (e.g. 1, c(1, 3), 3) to show only selected groups. Only works when group is specified.
title.leg Titles for legend groups. Can match the number of shown legends positionally, or supply titles for all groups (default = “Group”, “Group 2”, “Group 3”).
leg.args Named list of legend styling options: cex (default 0.75), horiz (default FALSE), x (optional x-coordinate), y (optional y-coordinate), title (optional title(s) if title.leg is omitted).
f1 Run a custom zero-argument function before the main plot (e.g. f1 = function() supergrid(col = "grey")).
f2 Run a custom zero-argument function before the variables plot.
… Additional arguments passed to plot() (main plot only), chull.args, or deprecated v1.x arguments.

Backwards Compatibility (v1.x to v2.0.0)

In betterbiplot 2.0.0, fine-grained styling arguments were grouped into lab.args, var.args, ellipse.args (or chull.args), and leg.args, and pc1/pc2 were combined into pc = c(1, 2). Legacy v1.x argument names continue to work via a soft deprecation shim that emits a warning pointing to the new syntax.

Before (v1.x):

bb_biplot(
  p, pc1 = 1, pc2 = 3, scale = 0, group = gr,
  lab_rotation = TRUE, whichv = "circle.eq", circle.eq = TRUE,
  col.v = "navy", expand = 1.2,
  ellipse = TRUE, se = 1, nofill = TRUE,
  legend = TRUE, title.leg = "Species", horiz = TRUE, lpx = -3.2
)

After (v2.0.0):

bb_biplot(
  p, pc = c(1, 3), scale = 0, group = gr,
  lab.args = list(rotate = TRUE),
  circle.eq = TRUE, var.args = list(which = "circle.eq", col = "navy", expand = 1.2),
  ellipse = TRUE, ellipse.args = list(level = 0.95, nofill = TRUE),
  legend = TRUE, title.leg = "Species", leg.args = list(horiz = TRUE, x = -3.2)
)
v1.x Argument v2.0.0 Equivalent
pc1, pc2 pc = c(pc1, pc2)
col.labd, cex.labd, font.labd lab.args = list(col = ..., cex = ..., font = ...)
lab_rotation, ran_adj, valign lab.args = list(rotate = ..., ran.adj = ..., valign = ...)
vname, whichv, expand, arrow.len var.args = list(vname = ..., which = ..., expand = ..., arrow.len = ...)
lwd.v, col.v, col.labv, cex.labv, font.labv, axes.v var.args = list(lwd = ..., col = ..., col.lab = ..., cex.lab = ..., font.lab = ..., axes = ...)
autolim, nofill, lwd.e ellipse.args = list(...) (or chull.args = list(...))
angle, se Removed (ellipses now use ellipse.args = list(method = "cov", level = 0.95))
cex.leg, horiz, lpx, lpy leg.args = list(cex = ..., horiz = ..., x = ..., y = ...)
f1.a, f2.a Wrapper function, e.g. f1 = function() fn(...)
